comparison: Perfect alignment on claims C30-C31, C37-C38, C40, C45-C46 characterizing PC-output relationships and dimensionality differences between regimes. Both evaluations find these geometric characterizations well-supported without challenge.
Perfect alignment on claim C21 regarding feedforward network background. Both accept this as appropriate contextualization of prior work (Chizat et al., 2019; Jacot et al., 2018).

Strong alignment on claims C26-C27, C52-C58 regarding heterogeneity and solution diversity in oblique regime. Both evaluations support the dissimilarity findings and mechanistic explanations. OpenEval additionally covers C6 which peer review addresses separately in R11.

Strong alignment on claims C7, C28, C70-C72, C74, C77-C79 regarding noise suppression mechanisms. Both evaluations support the variance ratio measurements and negative feedback explanations. OpenEval additionally covers C73, C75 which peer review addresses in R8 and R14.

Strong alignment on claims C63-C69 regarding differential perturbation responses. Both evaluations support the relative susceptibility findings and theoretical predictions. OpenEval additionally covers C8, C62 which peer review addresses separately in R11 and R14.

Both address core finding of two dynamical regimes (C4, C17-C18). OpenEval finds support from Figures 1-3 data. Peer review emphasizes all three reviewers explicitly affirm this as 'genuinely insightful.' Peer review R1 additionally covers C5, C19-C20 which OpenEval addresses in R3.

Both address claims C41-C44 regarding output weight magnitude persistence and generalization across tasks. OpenEval finds systematic relationship supported by Figure 3A. Peer review emphasizes strength of generalization across diverse tasks. OpenEval additionally covers C5, C19-C20 which peer review addresses in R1.

Both address claims C23-C24, C50-C51 regarding counter-rotating vs. co-rotating dynamics in cycling task. OpenEval finds clear visual evidence in Figure 2B. Peer review highlights this as key strength connecting theory to experimental observations. OpenEval additionally covers C32-C33 which peer review addresses in R12.

Both address background claims C11-C16 regarding neural representations and current knowledge limitations. Both evaluations accept these as well-established context supported by citations. OpenEval additionally covers C1-C3 which peer review also addresses in R15.

Both address theoretical predictions C34-C36 regarding correlation compensation for output weight magnitude. OpenEval emphasizes mathematical soundness and Methods analysis. Peer review notes the framework becomes 'obvious' once written out (Eq 3), marking it as genuinely insightful.

Critical divergence on claims C10, C29, C89 regarding BCI neural data analysis. OpenEval finds support from Figure 7 correlation measures but acknowledges dataset limitations. Peer review raises major weakness: BCI alignment may be confounded by experimental design where outputs are chosen to align with largest PCs. Reviewer 1 states 'connections to neural data were weak.'

Both address claims C80-C81, C84 connecting findings to prior experimental observations (Russo et al. 2018). OpenEval finds agreement strengthens findings. Peer review treats this as key validation that 'potentially unifies' experimental results. OpenEval R12 also covers C10, C29, C89 which peer review questions in R9.

Both address claims C9, C22 regarding theoretical analysis of recurrent vs. feedforward networks and learning dynamics. OpenEval emphasizes Figure 9 demonstrations and Methods analysis. Peer review praises 'deep analytical investigation' of regime evolution and training dynamics, including noise requirement (C47, C49, C73).

Both address claims C47, C49 regarding noise requirement for stable oblique solutions. OpenEval finds support in Figure 9 and theoretical justification. Peer review calls this 'an insightful corollary result,' treating it as key contribution. Peer R8 also covers broader theoretical analysis (C9, C22, C34, C73).

Both address mechanistic claims C59-C62 regarding RNN feedback dynamics. OpenEval finds support in established knowledge and Methods analysis. Peer review accepts these as part of 'deep analytical investigation' providing valid mechanistic insight. Peer R14 also covers C75.

Both address claim C25 regarding decoupling implications. OpenEval treats it as logical inference from demonstrated geometry. Peer review implicitly accepts this within framework understanding 'when dynamics do and do not align with target output.' Peer R11 also covers C6, C8 which OpenEval addresses in R8 and R9.

Both address claims C32-C33 regarding analytical implications of regime differences. OpenEval treats these as logical inferences supported by literature. Peer review implicitly accepts these implications as following from the accepted regime distinction.

Both address background claims C1-C3 regarding neural representations and dissociations. OpenEval finds these supported by general scientific consensus. Peer review accepts these as standard background establishing study motivation. Peer R15 also covers C11-C16.

Partial overlap on claims C5, C19-C20 regarding output weight magnitude relationship to regime. OpenEval R3 emphasizes systematic relationship across tasks (Figure 3A). Peer R1 focuses more on core regime distinction (C4, C17-C18) but encompasses these weight-related claims.
